title.en: Export and import procedures and documents

hook.en: A container of Indian spices reaches Rotterdam only after a dozen documents have been prepared, checked and signed. Each one has a purpose.

narration.en: A container of Indian spices reaches Rotterdam only after a dozen documents have been prepared, checked and signed. Each one has a purpose.

body.en: Main steps: receipt of an enquiry and an order (indent); checking the importer's creditworthiness, usually by asking for a letter of credit from his bank; obtaining an Importer–Exporter Code (IEC) from the DGFT and any licence needed; arranging pre-shipment finance; producing or procuring the goods; pre-shipment inspection where required; obtaining a certificate of origin; reserving shipping space; packing, marking and appointing a clearing and forwarding agent; insuring the goods; customs clearance (shipping bill); obtaining the mate's receipt and then the bill of lading after paying freight; preparing the invoice; and securing payment by presenting the documents through banks.

steps.en: Receive an order from the foreign buyer
Obtain a letter of credit and the IEC

Clear customs with the shipping bill
Load the goods and obtain the bill of lading
Send the documents through banks and receive payment

explanation.en: Order, assurance of payment, goods, shipping arrangements, customs, shipment, payment.

body.en: Letter of credit: a bank's guarantee to pay the exporter if the documents are in order. Bill of lading: issued by the shipping company, an acknowledgement of goods received for shipment and a document of title. Shipping bill: the main document for customs clearance of exports. Bill of entry: the importer's document for customs clearance of imports. Certificate of origin: shows where the goods were made (for duty concessions). Mate's receipt: given by the ship's officer when goods are loaded. Commercial invoice: the bill for the goods.

problem.en: Why does an exporter insist on a letter of credit?

steps.en: The buyer is far away, in another country, and may be unknown.
A letter of credit is the importer's bank's undertaking to pay.
Payment is made when the exporter presents the specified documents.
This removes the risk of non-payment.

answer.en: It guarantees payment by a bank, removing the risk of default.
